subject: Urgent: Veridian latency & error surge — exec review requested
messages:
From: Helen Zhou <helen.zhou@veridian.health>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@veridian.health; Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@veridian.health>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency and 5xx spike this morning — need remediation + credits

Ben,

We had a significant regresssion in our production workflows this morning between 08:20 and 09:05 PT. Our ingest onward pipeline saw elevated tail latency (p95 went from ~220ms to ~1.6s) and intermittent 5xx responses (~3.2% of requests) that caused retries and backpressure. This impacted three downstream services and triggered an incident in Veridian's ops runbook.

Can you confirm root cause and share the incident report, plus your proposed compensation for the SLA breach? Procurement needs an initial figure to start internal approvals. We are trying to avoid an immediate executive escalation but will escalate if we do not have a plan within 48 hours.

Attached is our observability snapshot and a consolidated error sample.

— Helen
Director, Engineering Operations
Veridian Health

Attachments: veridian_observability_0602.json (referenced)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Zhou <helen.zhou@veridian.health>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike this morning — need remediation + credits

Helen —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the observability snapshot. I'm sorry for the disruption this morning. We kicked off a full incident response as soon as we observed the elevated error rate and latency. Grace (CS) and our on-call infra team are already investigating. Initial findings: a regressive routing decision caused a subset of requests to land on a warm node pool that had degraded kernel performance after a recent kernel update; this impacted KV-cache hit patterns and caused transient queuing.

Immediate next steps:
- Internal RCA and incident report (I will deliver by EOD today).
- Temporary routing override to route Veridian traffic to the stable pool (already applied at 09:45 PT).
- Suggested initial credit for impacted window: our baseline proposal is to apply a 20% credit to June usage for the affected request class while we finish the RCA.

Would you be available for a 30-min exec call tomorrow 06/03 to walk through the incident and the credit schedule? I will include our ops lead and legal if needed.

Ben
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0189

Attachment: svc_incident_report_20270602.pdf (draft)

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Veridian incident — ops notes + escalation recommendation

Ben / Markus / Naomi —

Summary of ops findings (from infra on-call):
- Window: 2027-06-02T08:18–09:06 PT
- Symptoms: p95 latency rising to ~1.6s, 5xx rate peaked at 3.2% (client-facing), request queuing observed on affected warm pool nodes.
- Root cause (preliminary): kernel patch + a suboptimal kernel-optimized assembly path that regressed for this model family on certain GPU drivers. The runtime routed a small percentage of Veridian traffic to the affected pool because autoscaler placement hit capacity thresholds.
- Mitigation taken: routing override + rolling re-provision to stable kernel image. Incident closed at 09:55 PT.

Commercial recommendation:
- Offer a credit schedule tied to the incident window. Given Veridian's committed throughput and impact, propose: 20% credit on June invoice for the request class observed, capped at $25k, plus a one-time goodwill credit of $5k to cover Veridian's engineering remediation costs.
- Move to a Dedicated pool for Veridian as a medium-term mitigation; commercial to outline pricing delta and migration plan.

I recommend escalating to Naomi since Veridian may request an executive-level pledge on capacity locality and a legal SLA amendment.

Grace
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_credit_schedule_v2.xlsx

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Zhou <helen.zhou@veridian.health>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@veridian.health
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike this morning — need remediation + credits

Helen —

Appreciate the patience while we triaged. I want to get ahead of any exec escalations and propose we schedule a 45-minute call tomorrow (06/04) with our CTO and Naomi on our side to review the technical mitigation and the commercial package. Proposed agenda: incident recap, credits & timelines, Dedicated migration option, SLA amendment summary, next steps for procurement.

On credits: we are prepared to apply the 20% incident credit (cap as described) immediately as an invoice adjustment pending Veridian's acceptance of the proposed settlement. We will also provide the full incident packet (for your legal/procurement review) and a runbook entry describing the preventive steps.

If you prefer, we can escalate to legal to draft a short amendment that memorializes the credits and the Dedicated migration milestones; that will expedite procurement sign-off.

Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/rdw/Veridian/exec-brief-20270604

From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@veridian.health>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helen Zhou <helen.zhou@veridian.health>, procurement@veridian.health, naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and 5xx spike this morning — need remediation + credits

Markus / Ben —

Thank you — Veridian leadership reviewed your incident packet and preliminary credit proposal this afternoon. We appreciate the routing fix and the transparency. A few notes from procurement & legal:
- Procurement is fine with the 20% per-class credit for June, subject to receipt of the invoice adjustment and the final incident packet.
- Legal requests a short amendment that records the credit application and a commitment to a migration timeline to a Dedicated pool (if Veridian signs up for Dedicated, expected timeline 6–8 weeks). They asked for proposed amendment language and a redline.
- Exec ask: our CTO wants an explicit operational pledge around kernel image compatibility testing for our production model families; would Redwood be willing to include a statement about a pre-deploy compatibility validation for critical kernel updates for our Dedicated migration?

We are tentatively good to move forward with the credit and migration discussion pending Naomi/your legal draft. Can Redwood provide: final incident report, invoice adjustment, credit application mechanics, and a draft amendment by EOD Monday 06/07?

— Emma Lawson
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Veridian Health
